nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a real sequence indexed by $\{0, \dots, N-1\}$, let $k \ge 1$, and let $\varphi$ be a decreasing subsequence of $f$ of length $k$, that is, indices $\varphi(0) < \dots < \varphi(k-1)$ with $f(\varphi(0)) > \dots > f(\varphi(k-1))$, whose last index is $\varphi(k-1) = q$. If $p$ is an index with $q < p$ and $f(p) < f(q)$, then $f$ has a decreasing subsequence of length $k + 1$ that ends at $p$.
nodes.title: Extending a decreasing subsequence

nodes.summary: For every real sequence $f$ indexed by $\{0, \dots, N-1\}$ and every index $p$, the length of the longest strictly decreasing subsequence of $f$ ending at $p$ is at least $1$.
nodes.title: The longest decreasing subsequence ending at a point has length at least one

nodes.summary: For every real sequence $f$ indexed by $\{0, \dots, N-1\}$ and every index $p$, $f$ has a strictly decreasing subsequence ending at $p$ whose length equals the length of the longest strictly decreasing subsequence of $f$ ending at $p$.
nodes.title: The longest decreasing subsequence ending at a point is attained

nodes.summary: For a real sequence $f$ indexed by $\{0, \dots, N-1\}$ and an index $p$, this is the largest $k$ such that $f$ has a strictly decreasing subsequence of length $k$ ending at $p$, that is, indices $i_1 < \dots < i_k = p$ with $f(i_1) > \dots > f(i_k)$. The maximum exists: $k = 1$ qualifies, and every such $k$ is at most $N$.
nodes.title: Length of the longest decreasing subsequence ending at a point

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a real sequence indexed by $\{0, \dots, N-1\}$, and let $q < p$ be indices with $f(p) < f(q)$. Then the length of the longest strictly decreasing subsequence of $f$ ending at $q$ is strictly less than the length of the longest strictly decreasing subsequence of $f$ ending at $p$.
nodes.title: Longest decreasing subsequence lengths grow along a descent

nodes.summary: Let $r, s \ge 1$ be natural numbers, let $N = (r - 1)(s - 1) + 1$, and let $f$ be an injective real sequence indexed by $\{0, \dots, N-1\}$. Then $f$ has a strictly increasing subsequence of length $r$, that is, indices $i_1 < \dots < i_r$ with $f(i_1) < \dots < f(i_r)$, or a strictly decreasing subsequence of length $s$, that is, indices $j_1 < \dots < j_s$ with $f(j_1) > \dots > f(j_s)$.
nodes.title: Erdős–Szekeres theorem

nodes.summary: Let $k \ge 1$ and let $\varphi : \{0, \dots, k-1\} \to \{0, \dots, N-1\}$ be strictly increasing with last value $\varphi(k-1) = q$. If $p$ is an index with $q < p$, then the map on $\{0, \dots, k\}$ obtained by appending $p$ to $\varphi$, which sends each $i < k$ to $\varphi(i)$ and sends $k$ to $p$, is strictly increasing.
nodes.title: Appending a later index keeps indices increasing

nodes.summary: For every map $\varphi : \{0, \dots, k-1\} \to \{0, \dots, N-1\}$ and every $p \in \{0, \dots, N-1\}$, the map obtained by appending $p$ to $\varphi$ takes the value $p$ at its last index $k$.
nodes.title: The last entry of an appended map

nodes.summary: Given $\varphi : \{0, \dots, k-1\} \to \{0, \dots, N-1\}$ and $p \in \{0, \dots, N-1\}$, the appended map on $\{0, \dots, k\}$ sends each $i < k$ to $\varphi(i)$ and sends $k$ to $p$.
nodes.title: Appending an entry to a map of indices

nodes.summary: There are no $i, j \in \{0\}$ with $i < j$.
nodes.title: No strict pair in a one-element set

nodes.summary: Let $k \ge 1$ and let $\varphi : \{0, \dots, k-1\} \to \{0, \dots, N-1\}$ be strictly increasing with $\varphi(k-1) = q$. Then $\varphi(i) \le q$ for every $i < k$.
nodes.title: Entries of a strictly increasing index map lie at or below its last entry

nodes.summary: Let $f : \{0, \dots, N-1\} \to \mathbb{R}$, let $k \ge 1$, and let $\varphi$ be an increasing subsequence of $f$ of length $k$ (indices and values strictly increasing) with last index $\varphi(k-1) = q$. If $p \in \{0, \dots, N-1\}$ satisfies $q < p$ and $f(q) < f(p)$, then $f$ has an increasing subsequence of length $k + 1$ ending at $p$.
nodes.title: Extending an increasing subsequence

nodes.summary: For every $f : \{0, \dots, N-1\} \to \mathbb{R}$ and every position $p$, the length of the longest increasing subsequence of $f$ ending at $p$ is at least $1$.
nodes.title: Longest increasing subsequences ending at a position have length at least one

nodes.summary: For every $f : \{0, \dots, N-1\} \to \mathbb{R}$ and every position $p$, $f$ has an increasing subsequence ending at $p$ whose length equals the length of the longest increasing subsequence of $f$ ending at $p$.
nodes.title: The longest increasing subsequence ending at a position is attained

nodes.summary: For $f : \{0, \dots, N-1\} \to \mathbb{R}$ and a position $p$, this is the largest $k \le N$ such that $f$ has an increasing subsequence of length $k$ ending at $p$, where indices and values both increase strictly.
nodes.title: Length of the longest increasing subsequence ending at a position

nodes.summary: Let $f : \{0, \dots, N-1\} \to \mathbb{R}$ and let $q < p$ be positions with $f(q) < f(p)$. Then the length of the longest increasing subsequence of $f$ ending at $q$ is strictly less than the length of the longest increasing subsequence of $f$ ending at $p$.
nodes.title: Longest increasing subsequence lengths increase strictly along increasing pairs

nodes.summary: For $f : \{0, \dots, N-1\} \to \mathbb{R}$, a position $p$ and $k \in \mathbb{N}$, this is the statement that $k \ge 1$ and $f$ has a decreasing subsequence $\varphi$ of length $k$ (indices strictly increasing and values strictly decreasing) ending at $p$, that is, with $\varphi(k-1) = p$.
nodes.title: Decreasing subsequence ending at a position

nodes.summary: For $f : \{0, \dots, N-1\} \to \mathbb{R}$ and $k \in \mathbb{N}$, a map $\varphi : \{0, \dots, k-1\} \to \{0, \dots, N-1\}$ is a decreasing subsequence of $f$ of length $k$ when $\varphi(i) < \varphi(j)$ and $f(\varphi(j)) < f(\varphi(i))$ for all $i < j$.
nodes.title: Decreasing subsequence

nodes.summary: For $f : \{0, \dots, N-1\} \to \mathbb{R}$, a position $p$ and $k \in \mathbb{N}$, this is the statement that $k \ge 1$ and $f$ has an increasing subsequence $\varphi$ of length $k$ (indices and values strictly increasing) ending at $p$, that is, with $\varphi(k-1) = p$.
nodes.title: Increasing subsequence ending at a position

nodes.summary: For $f : \{0, \dots, N-1\} \to \mathbb{R}$ and $k \in \mathbb{N}$, a map $\varphi : \{0, \dots, k-1\} \to \{0, \dots, N-1\}$ is an increasing subsequence of $f$ of length $k$ when $\varphi(i) < \varphi(j)$ and $f(\varphi(i)) < f(\varphi(j))$ for all $i < j$.
nodes.title: Increasing subsequence

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a real sequence indexed by $\{0, \dots, N-1\}$, let $k \ge 1$, and let $\varphi$ map $\{0, \dots, k-1\}$ to $\{0, \dots, N-1\}$ so that $f(\varphi(j)) < f(\varphi(i))$ whenever $i < j < k$. If $\varphi(k-1) = q$, then $f(q) \le f(\varphi(i))$ for every $i < k$.
nodes.title: The last value is the smallest along a strictly decreasing selection

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a real sequence indexed by $\{0, \dots, N-1\}$ and let $p$ be a position. If $f$ has a strictly decreasing subsequence of length $k$ ending exactly at $p$, then $k$ is at most the length of the longest strictly decreasing subsequence of $f$ ending at $p$.
nodes.title: Bound by the longest decreasing subsequence ending at a position

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a real sequence indexed by $\{0, \dots, N-1\}$ and let $p$ be a position. If $f$ has a strictly increasing subsequence of length $k$ ending exactly at $p$, then $k$ is at most the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence of $f$ ending at $p$.
nodes.title: Bound by the longest increasing subsequence ending at a position

nodes.summary: For every real sequence $f$ indexed by $\{0, \dots, N-1\}$ and every position $p$, the subsequence of length $1$ consisting of the term at position $p$ is a strictly decreasing subsequence of $f$.
nodes.title: One-term subsequences are decreasing

nodes.summary: For every real sequence $f$ indexed by $\{0, \dots, N-1\}$ and every position $p$, the subsequence of length $1$ consisting of the term at position $p$ is a strictly increasing subsequence of $f$.
nodes.title: One-term subsequences are increasing

nodes.summary: For every natural number $k > 0$, $k - 1 < k$.
nodes.title: A positive natural number exceeds its predecessor

nodes.summary: If $\varphi \colon \{0, \dots, k-1\} \to \{0, \dots, N-1\}$ is strictly increasing, that is $\varphi(i) < \varphi(j)$ whenever $i < j$, then $k \le N$.
nodes.title: Subsequences are no longer than the sequence

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a real sequence indexed by $\{0, \dots, N-1\}$. If $f$ has a strictly decreasing subsequence of length $k$, then for every $s \le k$ it has a strictly decreasing subsequence of length $s$.
nodes.title: Decreasing subsequences of every smaller length

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a real sequence indexed by $\{0, \dots, N-1\}$. If $f$ has a strictly increasing subsequence of length $k$, then for every $r \le k$ it has a strictly increasing subsequence of length $r$.
nodes.title: Increasing subsequences of every smaller length

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a real sequence indexed by $\{0, \dots, N-1\}$, let $k \ge 1$, and let $\varphi$ map $\{0, \dots, k-1\}$ to $\{0, \dots, N-1\}$ so that $f(\varphi(i)) < f(\varphi(j))$ whenever $i < j < k$. If $\varphi(k-1) = q$, then $f(\varphi(i)) \le f(q)$ for every $i < k$.
nodes.title: The last value is the largest along a strictly increasing selection

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
